source.title: How Do LLMs Use Their Depth?
source.authors: Akshat Gupta; Jay Yeung; G. Anumanchipalli; Anna A. Ivanova

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It contains minor typographical errors, but no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports multi-token fact-recall results and interprets later answer tokens as conditionally easier to predict than the first token. This offers a local conditional-ease account relevant to V6, but it does not directly test future-token representations or causal steering.
record.gate_note: The study measures layerwise token ranks for fact recall, including comparisons between answer-token positions. These results bear on V6's alternative local-feature explanation, but do not measure a future token represented at an earlier token position or intervene on such a representation. Its other results on frequency-conditioned guesses, POS, and option-constrained tasks do not test the listed versions. The paper cites prior lookahead work; those cited findings are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Each answer token is tracked with TunedLens only at the position where it is predicted, so this is ordinary next-token emergence depth. No future token is decoded from an earlier hidden state (V2). No feature is shown to be computed for later positions (V3). No plan is probed or steered (V1, V4, V5), and no apparent plan is examined for shallowness or local explanation (V6). The authors only speculate that the first token must 'anticipate the future tokens'. They cite lookahead work in related work but report no rate or strength of look-ahead.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say the first token of a correct multi-token fact needs the most depth and later tokens emerge earlier because they are conditionally easier given the first. They also speculate, without testing, that multi-token facts are harder because the model must anticipate the future tokens. The paper's overall conclusion is the Guess-then-Refine framework and complexity-driven depth use, not a claim about planning.
record.recipe_differences: Uses TunedLens layerwise token-rank tracking and related depth analyses, not rhyme-word interventions or causal editing of future-token representations.
record.method_sensitivity: The fact-recall analysis is restricted to prompts where the model generated the correct answer. The paper states that incorrect factual recalls show a somewhat different pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: In correct multi-token fact recall, the first answer token reaches a given TunedLens rank at deeper layers than single-token answers. Later answer tokens emerge much shallower (Pythia-6.9B, 3-token facts: about layer 27 vs 20 vs 12). For incorrect recalls, multi-token first tokens no longer need more depth than single-token answers (Appendix H).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: First tokens of multi-token answers need more layerwise computation than later tokens; possibly linked to committing to a multi-token continuation.

record.problems: Fact-recall analyses include only prompts where the model produced the correct answer; the paper gives counts by model and answer position in Table 1. Reported layer values have no uncertainty estimates in the text. The layer-rank threshold associated with the textual summary is not stated, and the results do not directly intervene on or test future-token planning.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant numerical fact-recall results are stated in text. Other model and threshold results are shown in figures without textual values and are not separately extracted.

untested.parts: No rhyming verse, frontier model or intervention.
No decoding of tokens several positions ahead from a single hidden state.
No test of features computed for the benefit of later positions.
No rhyme planning in open models.
No look-ahead measured in any task.
No apparent plan is identified, so neither its horizon nor its explanation by local features is tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'challenges' label is removed. Later tokens being easier once earlier tokens are in context is ordinary autoregressive conditioning, not evidence against a steering plan. No measurement of future-token content at earlier positions was made.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme-word representation, or intervention changing a verse ending.
Does not measure whether a single hidden state predicts tokens several positions ahead.
Does not test whether a feature is computed at one token position because it helps later positions rather than as a next-token side effect.
No rhyme-planning test using open-weight models or attribution-graph/probing tools.
No test of look-ahead in multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other listed tasks and architectures.
The fact-recall analysis covers correct answers with up to three answer tokens; it does not directly measure planning horizon, local next-token features, or causal steering of intermediate text.

rows.subject: Pythia-6.9B

rows.measure: Earliest appearance of the correct fact-recall token

rows.note: The paper reports the single-token answer's first appearance at layer 15; the rank threshold for this textual summary is not stated.
rows.check: Layer at which a single-token answer emerges at its own position. This is next-token depth use, not a future-token representation or a test of plan shallowness.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Discusses prior look-ahead research and speculates about anticipating later fact tokens, without measuring future-token representations or a plan that steers generation.

tranche.reason: Measures layerwise emergence of the next token at each answer position. It neither tests nor uses the planning mechanisms named by the claim versions.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v2, dated March 2026. Reported emergence depths concern correct fact recalls; the numerical summaries do not specify a rank threshold.

reader_labels.condition: Correct MQuAKE fact-recall answers, including three-token answers; reported examples for Pythia-6.9B and Llama3-8B
reader_labels.reason: Later answer tokens emerge at shallower layers than the first, and the authors describe them as conditionally easier given the first token; this is consistent with a local conditional-ease account rather than demonstrating a plan that steers generation (R1–R7).
